methodological_rigor.justification: Single-center, single-arm, open-label phase II with a formal sample-size calculation (ORR null 47%, alternative 65%, one-sided alpha 0.05, 80% power, n>=52) and prespecified ITT analysis. RECIST 1.1 was used, tumor assessments scheduled every 6-9 weeks, and LASSO penalized logistic/Cox multivariable analyses appropriately addressed overfitting. Principal weaknesses are the absence of a control arm (acknowledged), single-center recruitment, small subgroup sizes, and inability to separate tislelizumab contribution from XELOX/bevacizumab. Biomarker flow-cytometry analyses are exploratory and underpowered.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual phase II cohort trial in the classically ICI-resistant MSS/pMMR RAS-mutant mCRC population, mapping to Oxford LoE 2b. The 73.1% ORR, 98.1% DCR, and 9.6-month PFS with manageable toxicity (21.2% grade >=3 TRAE, no treatment-related deaths) are clinically meaningful hypothesis-generating signals, particularly the KRAS G13D subgroup (ORR 84.6%, PFS 12.8 months), and are explicitly framed as rationale for a phase III trial.

reporting_quality.justification: Single-arm phase II is usually reported under CONSORT extensions; CONSORT is not explicitly cited but the manuscript includes a study schema (Fig 1), prespecified endpoints, trial registration (NCT05970302), sample-size justification, safety reporting, and detailed eligibility/treatment procedures. Limitations are openly discussed. Individual-level data are not shared and no repository deposition is mentioned; supplementary URLs are redacted in this version.

novelty_literature.justification: The strategy of combining anti-PD-1 with chemo plus bevacizumab in MSS/pMMR mCRC has been explored (AtezoTRIBE, NIVACOR, BBCAPX, CheckMate 9X8), which the authors extensively cite and compare against. Specific novelty is the tislelizumab + XELOX + bevacizumab combination enriched for RAS-mutant patients and a KRAS G13D subgroup signal, plus peripheral immune-cell biomarker exploration. This is a meaningful extension rather than a field-defining discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly structured, with prespecified endpoints, a detailed methods section, descriptive baseline table, response figures (waterfall/spider/swimmer/KM), and multivariable forest plots. Discussion thoughtfully contextualizes results against AtezoTRIBE, NIVACOR, BBCAPX and CheckMate 9X8. Some minor inconsistencies appear (e.g., 'KRAS G12S1 (19.2)' in Table 1 seems mislabeled) and the abstract mentions 200 mg/m2 tislelizumab where the methods specify 200 mg flat dose.

key_strengths: Prespecified phase II with formal sample-size calculation met its primary ORR endpoint (73.1%, 95% CI 61.1-85.1)
Targets an unmet-need population (MSS/pMMR RAS-mutant mCRC) classically resistant to ICIs
Favorable safety profile (21.2% grade >=3 TRAE, no treatment-related deaths) versus FOLFOXIRI-based triplets
LASSO-penalized multivariable analyses for subgroup exploration; peripheral-blood biomarker signals are hypothesis-generating
Transparent comparison against contemporaneous trials (AtezoTRIBE, NIVACOR, BBCAPX, CheckMate 9X8)
key_concerns: Single-arm, single-center design precludes causal attribution of benefit to tislelizumab
Median PFS (9.6 months) is not superior to historical FOLFOXIRI-bev (11.1 months) or to contemporary trials (BBCAPX 17.9 months; serplulimab-XELOX 17.2 months)
Small subgroup sizes (e.g., G13D n=13) render biomarker and KRAS-subtype findings hypothesis-generating only
Discrepancy between abstract dose ('200 mg/m2') and methods ('200 mg flat') should be corrected
No individual patient data or biomarker data sharing statement visible
chief_reviewer.rationale: A well-designed single-arm phase II with a strong ORR signal in a difficult-to-treat population, but lack of control arm, modest PFS relative to contemporaneous trials, and internal inconsistencies justify tier 2 with major revisions rather than tier 1.
